title: Futex (Fast Userspace Mutex)
summary: A futex is a Linux synchronization primitive: a 32-bit integer in user space. Operations: FUTEX_WAIT (if value == expected, sleep), FUTEX_WAKE (wake N waiters), FUTEX_WAIT_BITSET, FUTEX_WAKE_BITSET, FUTEX_REQUEUE (move waiters between futexes), FUTEX_CMP_REQUEUE, FUTEX_LOCK_PI (priority inheritance), FUTEX_UNLOCK_PI, FUTEX_TRYLOCK_PI, FUTEX_WAIT_REQUEUE_PI, FUTEX_CMP_REQUEUE_PI. The kernel is only involved on contention (slow path). Uncontended lock/unlock is pure userspace (atomic CAS).

structure.meaning: The 32-bit integer in user space. Value semantics: 0 = unlocked, 1 = locked (no waiters), 2 = locked (has waiters).
If *addr == val, sleep. Returns 0 on wake, -EAGAIN if val changed, -EINTR if interrupted.
Wake up to val waiters. Returns number woken.
Move waiters from one futex to another. Used for condition variables (wake one, requeue rest).
Lock with priority inheritance (real-time). Owner's priority is boosted to highest waiter's priority.
Uncontended lock: atomic CAS (0→1). Uncontended unlock: atomic store (1→0). No syscall.
Contention: syscall to kernel. Kernel maintains wait queue (rb-tree). Wakes waiters on unlock.

notes: Futexes are the foundation of all pthread synchronization (mutex, condvar, rwlock, barrier).
Uncontended futex operations are O(1) userspace (no syscall).
Contention requires a syscall (kernel wait queue).
futex2 (Linux 5.16+) adds waitv (wait on multiple futexes) and timeout improvements.
